item.title: The Sea at the Bottom of This Page
item.description:
You probably came here from the “how?” next to the record at the bottom of the page. This is what that sea is.

It’s an oil painting that nobody held a brush for. I drew a simple scene, a small program painted it stroke by stroke (curved strokes, bristles, a bit of impasto, linen underneath), and on the page only the water moves, band by band.

item.title: A Portrait That Listens to My Spotify and Judges Your Browser
item.description:
If you open the home page now, the portrait doesn’t just sit there anymore. It says hi, dresses up for whatever I’m listening to, takes a good look at you and tells you what it thinks, then does the Omarchy bit it always did. Every couple of seconds, by itself.

A made-up visit: someone in Germany, on Windows, at 2 am, while I play arabesk.

item.title: GAW GAW and the Jumping Poops
item.description:
The game my 5-year-old designed.

My daughter, like most 5 year olds, likes to play games on her iPad.

There was this long overdue idea in my head: build her a game that’s actually hers, and get some real hours together while doing it. I wouldn’t know much about game development apart from a couple of attempts with Flash when I was 12 at the end of the ’90s. So nothing much that’s transferable into 2026. But you know, we have Claude Code now and all the open-source tooling, the entry bar to game development shouldn’t be that high anymore.

item.title: If You Wouldn't Care Enough to Write It Yourself Why Would I Care Reading It
item.description: So I started creating a few journal entries with the help of ‘AI’. I began drafting a couple of sentences here and there using Typora coz I’m in love with it and scratched the pad with floating thoughts on my reMarkable with the aim of turning them into neat journal entries. Then I provided those to Claude and asked it to first learn my writing style from my past entries and then generate journal entries keeping my humor and authentic self. Didn’t like the outcome so I didn’t even publish them.
